learning_objective: 🎯 Dive into ecology to understand how organisms adapt to extreme environments and how populations grow, interact, and survive together!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Ecology studies interactions among organisms and their environment. Major abiotic (non-living) factors include temperature, water, light, and soil. Organisms respond by regulating (mammals sweating), conforming (lizards changing temp), migrating, or suspending (hibernation).

Traits that allow organisms to survive and reproduce. Kangaroo rats in deserts never drink water (they get it from fat oxidation). Desert plants have thick cuticles and sunken stomata to prevent water loss.
Populations have specific characteristics that individual organisms do not: Birth rates, death rates, sex ratios, and age pyramids (which show if a population is expanding, stable, or declining).

Exponential growth (J-shaped curve) happens when resources are unlimited. Logistic growth (S-shaped curve) is more realistic; it happens when limited resources cap the population at a maximum 'Carrying Capacity' (K).

Organisms rarely live alone. They interact! Mutualism (+/+, both benefit), Competition (-/-, both harmed), Predation and Parasitism (+/-, one benefits, one is harmed), Commensalism (+/0, one benefits, one unaffected).

fun_activity.title: 🦁 The Predator-Prey Dance
fun_activity.instructions: Think of a graph tracking lions and zebras. When zebras increase, lions get more food and their numbers increase. But more lions mean more zebras get eaten, so zebra numbers fall. Then lions starve and their numbers fall, allowing zebras to increase again. It's a never-ending natural cycle!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize the interaction table (+, -, 0). Commensalism (e.g., orchids on a mango tree) and Amensalism (-, 0) are frequently asked.
📌 Be able to draw and explain the Logistic Growth curve equation: $dN/dt = rN(K-N)/K$. Explain what 'K' (carrying capacity) means.
📌 Allen's Rule: Mammals from colder climates generally have shorter ears and limbs to minimize heat loss.
quick_recap: ⭐ Predators act as 'prudent' managers of nature; they keep prey populations under control and maintain species diversity.
⭐ Gause's 'Competitive Exclusion Principle' states that two closely related species competing for the exact same resources cannot co-exist indefinitely.
⭐ Endoparasites (living inside the host) generally have highly simplified anatomies but massive reproductive capacities.
